lemma: describe work with a connected detail
displayForm: I work as a graphic designer, and I work from home most days.

ru.translation: Я работаю графическим дизайнером и большую часть дней работаю из дома.

examples.text: I work as a graphic designer, and I work from home most days.

npcReplyCorrect: That must be convenient. Do you have any brothers or sisters?

displayForm: I have one sister, and we often cook dinner together.

ru.translation: У меня есть сестра, и мы часто готовим ужин вместе.

examples.text: I have one sister, and we often cook dinner together.

npcReplyCorrect: That sounds nice. What do you like doing in your free time?

lemma: connect an interest with a related local detail
displayForm: I play tennis at weekends. I've lived here for three years, so I know a couple of good courts.

ru.translation: По выходным я играю в теннис. Я живу здесь уже три года, поэтому знаю пару хороших кортов.
ru.usageNote: I've lived here for three years is a fixed lexical chunk; Present Perfect is not taught as a target here.

examples.text: I play tennis at weekends. I've lived here for three years, so I know a couple of good courts.

npcReplyCorrect: Three years is a good while. Which courts do you like best?

lemma: introduce different job and family details
displayForm: I'm a primary-school teacher, and I share a flat with my cousin.

ru.translation: Я учитель начальной школы и снимаю квартиру вместе с двоюродной сестрой.

examples.text: I'm a primary-school teacher, and I share a flat with my cousin.

npcReplyCorrect: Primary school must be lively. What do you and your cousin do together?

displayForm: We cook together most evenings, and I go swimming on Sundays.

ru.translation: Мы готовим вместе почти каждый вечер, а по воскресеньям я хожу плавать.

examples.text: We cook together most evenings, and I go swimming on Sundays.

npcReplyCorrect: That sounds like a lovely routine. How long have you lived in this neighbourhood?

lemma: say how long you have lived somewhere
displayForm: I've lived here for six months, but I still don't know many cafés.

ru.translation: Я живу здесь шесть месяцев, но пока знаю мало кафе.
ru.usageNote: I've lived here for six months is a fixed lexical chunk; Present Perfect is not taught as a target here.

examples.text: I've lived here for six months, but I still don't know many cafés.

npcReplyCorrect: In that case, I can recommend a little place near the park.

lemma: answer how you know a mutual friend
displayForm: Alex and I know each other from the café near my office.

ru.translation: Мы с Алексом знаем друг друга по кафе рядом с моим офисом.

examples.text: Alex and I know each other from the café near my office.

npcReplyCorrect: Small world—Alex knows everyone around here! What do you do?

lemma: share work and ask a social question
displayForm: I work in a small design office. What about you?

ru.translation: Я работаю в небольшом дизайнерском бюро. А ты?

examples.text: I work in a small design office. What about you?

npcReplyCorrect: I'm an architect. I spend most of my day drawing plans.

lemma: show interest with a follow-up question
displayForm: That sounds interesting. What do you enjoy most about your work?

ru.translation: Звучит интересно. Что тебе больше всего нравится в твоей работе?

examples.text: That sounds interesting. What do you enjoy most about your work?

npcReplyCorrect: I like seeing a design take shape. What do you like doing outside work?

lemma: connect with someone through a shared activity
displayForm: Alex and I are in the same weekend running group. We usually get coffee after the run.

ru.translation: Мы с Алексом ходим в одну беговую группу по выходным.

examples.text: Alex and I are in the same weekend running group. We usually get coffee after the run.

npcReplyCorrect: That sounds fun. How do you know Maya?

displayForm: Maya and I are in the same English class. We sit together.

ru.translation: Мы с Майей ходим в одну группу английского языка. Мы сидим вместе.

examples.text: Maya and I are in the same English class. We sit together.

npcReplyCorrect: That makes sense—Maya is good at bringing people together.

lemma: change an item in an order
displayForm: Actually, could I change this to a tea instead?

ru.translation: Слушай, можно я заменю кофе на чай?

examples.text: Actually, could I change this to a tea instead?

npcReplyCorrect: Of course. I haven't made it yet. Hot or iced?

displayForm: Hot, please. Can I have it large?

examples.text: Hot, please. Can I have it large?

npcReplyCorrect: Sure—a large hot tea. I'll update the order before you pay.

lemma: change the quantity in an order
displayForm: Actually, can I make that two teas instead of one?

ru.translation: Можно я изменю заказ: вместо одного чая будет два?

examples.text: Actually, can I make that two teas instead of one?

npcReplyCorrect: No problem. Two teas—the card reader is ready when you are.

lemma: change an order after payment starts
displayForm: Sorry, I've just tapped my card. Could I change that to three teas instead?

ru.translation: Извините, я только что приложила карту. Можно изменить заказ на три чая?
ru.usageNote: I've just tapped my card is a fixed Present Perfect chunk; no Present Perfect target is introduced here.

examples.text: Sorry, I've just tapped my card. Could I change that to three teas instead?

npcReplyCorrect: That's fine. I can cancel that payment and update the order to three teas.

displayForm: I'd like to book a table for Friday evening, please.

ru.translation: Я бы хотела забронировать столик на вечер пятницы, пожалуйста.

examples.text: I'd like to book a table for Friday evening, please.

npcReplyCorrect: Certainly. How many people is the table for?

lemma: give the party size and ask about a booking time
displayForm: Two, please. Is seven thirty available?

ru.translation: На двоих, пожалуйста. Можно на половину восьмого?

examples.text: Two, please. Is seven thirty available?

npcReplyCorrect: It is. What name should I put on the booking?

lemma: give the name for a booking
displayForm: Anna, please. That's A-N-N-A.

examples.text: Anna, please. That's A-N-N-A.

npcReplyCorrect: Thank you, Anna. You're booked for two at seven thirty on Friday.

lemma: book a different day and party size
displayForm: I'd like to book a table for four on Saturday, please.

ru.translation: Я бы хотела забронировать столик на субботу на четверых.

examples.text: I'd like to book a table for four on Saturday, please.

npcReplyCorrect: Certainly. I can offer six thirty or eight. Which time works for you?

lemma: choose a time and give the booking name
displayForm: Eight is good. The booking is under Anna.

ru.translation: Восемь подойдёт. Бронь на имя Анна.

examples.text: Eight is good. The booking is under Anna.

npcReplyCorrect: Great, a table for four at eight on Saturday, under Anna.

lemma: ask to repeat booking information on a phone call
displayForm: Sorry, could you repeat the available times? I'm calling to book for Sunday, and the line cut out.

ru.translation: Извините, повторите, пожалуйста, свободное время? Я звоню забронировать столик на воскресенье, связь прервалась.
ru.usageNote: Could you repeat is a fixed polite clarification chunk; the exchange is explicitly phone-only.

examples.text: Sorry, could you repeat the available times? I'm calling to book for Sunday, and the line cut out.

npcReplyCorrect: Of course. I can offer six fifteen or eight. Which time works for you?

displayForm: Eight, please. I'd like a table for four, and the name is Anna.

ru.translation: На восемь, пожалуйста. Столик на четверых, имя Анна.

examples.text: Eight, please. I'd like a table for four, and the name is Anna.

npcReplyCorrect: All set, Anna: four people at eight on Sunday.

lemma: ask if a dish contains an ingredient
displayForm: Are there any onions in the vegetable soup?

examples.text: Are there any onions in the vegetable soup?

npcReplyCorrect: Yes, there are. I can ask the kitchen to leave them out.

lemma: order a dish without one ingredient
displayForm: Two bowls without onions, please.

examples.text: Two bowls without onions, please.

npcReplyCorrect: Certainly. Anything else?

lemma: add a side to a group order
displayForm: Yes, please. Could we have some bread with it too?

ru.usageNote: Could we have is a fixed polite request chunk; some is used in the learner's positive request.

examples.text: Yes, please. Could we have some bread with it too?

npcReplyCorrect: Of course. I'll add bread for the table.

lemma: check whether a dish contains dairy
displayForm: Does the tomato pasta have any cream?

examples.text: Does the tomato pasta have any cream?

npcReplyCorrect: Yes, the sauce has cream. The kitchen can prepare it without cream.

lemma: request a dairy-free change to a dish
displayForm: Yes, please. Could we have it without cream?

ru.translation: Да, пожалуйста. Можно приготовить её без сливок?
ru.usageNote: Could we have is a fixed polite request chunk; the transfer is a dairy detail rather than a medical discussion.

examples.text: Yes, please. Could we have it without cream?

npcReplyCorrect: Of course. I'll ask the kitchen to leave the cream out.

lemma: increase a group order from two to four portions
displayForm: Could we have four bowls instead of two? And some bread for everyone, please.

ru.translation: Можно четыре порции вместо двух? И хлеб для всех, пожалуйста.
ru.usageNote: Could we have is a fixed polite request chunk; the transfer changes the group size and quantity.

examples.text: Could we have four bowls instead of two? And some bread for everyone, please.

npcReplyCorrect: Of course—four bowls and bread for everyone.

displayForm: Sorry I'm late. I missed the bus, and the next one isn't for twenty minutes.

ru.translation: Извини, я опоздала. Я пропустила автобус, а следующий будет только через двадцать минут.

examples.text: Sorry I'm late. I missed the bus, and the next one isn't for twenty minutes.

npcReplyCorrect: Oh no. Are you still at the bus stop?

lemma: ask what to do after a delay
displayForm: Yes. What should I do now? I don't want to miss our train.

ru.translation: Да. Что мне теперь делать? Я не хочу опоздать на наш поезд.

examples.text: Yes. What should I do now? I don't want to miss our train.

npcReplyCorrect: You should take a taxi to the station. I'll wait by the main entrance.

lemma: explain missing a meeting after going to the wrong building
displayForm: I'm sorry I'm late for the meeting. I went to the wrong building, so I missed it.

ru.translation: Извини, я опоздала на встречу. Я пошла не в то здание и пропустила её.

examples.text: I'm sorry I'm late for the meeting. I went to the wrong building, so I missed it.

npcReplyCorrect: Oh no. Is the meeting over now?

lemma: ask for a next step after missing a meeting
displayForm: Yes. What should I do now?

examples.text: Yes. What should I do now?

npcReplyCorrect: You should message the group and ask when they can meet again.

lemma: explain a personal delay that caused a missed train
displayForm: I'm sorry. I overslept because my alarm didn't ring, and we missed our early train.

ru.translation: Извини. Я проспала, потому что будильник не прозвенел, и мы опоздали на ранний поезд.

examples.text: I'm sorry. I overslept because my alarm didn't ring, and we missed our early train.

npcReplyCorrect: Oh, that's a shame. The next train leaves at twelve thirty. Do you still want to go today?

lemma: ask how to change a delayed travel plan
displayForm: Yes, let's go later. What should we do now?

ru.translation: Да, давай поедем позже. Что нам теперь делать?
ru.usageNote: Let's go later is a fixed suggestion chunk; should is recycled to ask for advice.

examples.text: Yes, let's go later. What should we do now?

npcReplyCorrect: You should call the hotel and tell them we'll arrive later.

lemma: check a direction you may have misheard
displayForm: Sorry, did you say turn right at the bridge?

ru.translation: Извините, вы сказали повернуть направо у моста?
ru.usageNote: Sorry, did you say...? is a clarification frame; turn right is intentionally checked because the direction was heard incorrectly.

examples.text: Sorry, did you say turn right at the bridge?

npcReplyCorrect: No, turn left at the bridge. After the library, turn right at the traffic lights.

lemma: repeat directions in your own words and confirm them
displayForm: So you said to turn left at the bridge, go past the library, then turn right at the lights. Is that right?

ru.translation: То есть вы сказали повернуть налево у моста, пройти библиотеку и повернуть направо у светофора. Я правильно поняла?
ru.usageNote: The learner actively reconstructs the route; reported confirmation is the situation's Grammar Target.

examples.text: So you said to turn left at the bridge, go past the library, then turn right at the lights. Is that right?

npcReplyCorrect: That's right. The museum is just across the next crossing, on your left.

lemma: confirm the last part of a route
displayForm: So I go straight across at the next crossing, and the museum is on my left?

ru.translation: То есть я иду прямо через следующий перекрёсток, и музей будет слева?
ru.usageNote: So I go... and Is that right? are short spoken route-checking chunks.

examples.text: So I go straight across at the next crossing, and the museum is on my left?

npcReplyCorrect: Exactly. You can't miss it.

lemma: restate a route with three turns
displayForm: So I go straight on, turn left at the park, pass the post office, turn right at the bridge, then take the first left. Is that right?

ru.translation: То есть я иду прямо, поворачиваю налево у парка, прохожу почту, направо у моста, а затем налево. Всё верно?
ru.usageNote: Transfers the same route-checking function to a longer route with three turns.

examples.text: So I go straight on, turn left at the park, pass the post office, turn right at the bridge, then take the first left. Is that right?

npcReplyCorrect: Yes, that's the route. After the third turn, the museum entrance is on your right.

lemma: clarify a bus number and confirm where to get off
displayForm: Sorry, did you say bus sixty? So I take the sixteen and get off by the market, is that right?

ru.translation: Извините, вы сказали автобус шестьдесят? То есть я еду на шестнадцатом и выхожу у рынка, верно?
ru.usageNote: The learner mishears sixty instead of sixteen, then checks the journey details.

examples.text: Sorry, did you say bus sixty? So I take the sixteen and get off by the market, is that right?

npcReplyCorrect: That's right—bus sixteen. It stops right by the market.

lemma: start a short story about a weekend event
displayForm: On Saturday, Maya and I watched a new film downtown.

ru.translation: В субботу мы с Майей посмотрели новый фильм в центре.

examples.text: On Saturday, Maya and I watched a new film downtown.

npcReplyCorrect: Did you enjoy it?

lemma: add a reaction and connect the next event
displayForm: Yes, it was funny, and we talked about it over dinner.

ru.translation: Да, было смешно, и мы обсуждали фильм за ужином.

examples.text: Yes, it was funny, and we talked about it over dinner.

npcReplyCorrect: Where did you have dinner?

lemma: finish a connected weekend story with an opinion
displayForm: We had a lovely dinner at the little Italian café beside the cinema.

ru.translation: Мы чудесно поужинали в небольшом итальянском кафе рядом с кинотеатром.
ru.usageNote: Past Simple actions and a simple evaluation keep the story coherent across turns.

examples.text: We had a lovely dinner at the little Italian café beside the cinema.

npcReplyCorrect: That sounds like a lovely evening. Thanks for telling me.

lemma: tell a different weekend story about a day trip
displayForm: On Saturday, I took a train to Bath with my cousin.

ru.translation: В субботу я поехала на поезде в Бат с двоюродной сестрой.
ru.usageNote: A different event and companion transfer the Past Simple story pattern.

examples.text: On Saturday, I took a train to Bath with my cousin.

npcReplyCorrect: Oh, nice. What did you do there?

lemma: connect events and give a weekend reaction
displayForm: We visited the market and had lunch by the river. It was a lovely day.

ru.translation: Мы сходили на рынок и пообедали у реки. День был чудесный.

examples.text: We visited the market and had lunch by the river. It was a lovely day.

npcReplyCorrect: That sounds like a good day out.

displayForm: We planned a picnic, but it rained all morning, so we stayed at the museum café instead.

ru.translation: Мы планировали пикник, но всё утро шёл дождь, поэтому вместо этого мы остались в кафе при музее.
ru.usageNote: A simple weather problem changes the event and requires a connected Past Simple response.

examples.text: We planned a picnic, but it rained all morning, so we stayed at the museum café instead.

npcReplyCorrect: At least the museum café kept you dry. Did you enjoy the exhibition?

lemma: share a plan for next week
displayForm: I'm going to visit the art market after work next week.

ru.translation: На следующей неделе я собираюсь после работы сходить на арт-маркет.

examples.text: I'm going to visit the art market after work next week.

npcReplyCorrect: Oh, nice. Which day? I finish early on Thursday.

lemma: arrange a time and place to meet
displayForm: Thursday works. I'm meeting you at the station at six, and we're walking over together.

ru.translation: В четверг удобно. Мы встречаемся у вокзала в шесть и пойдём туда вместе.
ru.usageNote: Present Continuous is used for the confirmed arrangement with Alex.

examples.text: Thursday works. I'm meeting you at the station at six, and we're walking over together.

npcReplyCorrect: Perfect. What would you like to do after the market?

lemma: add a second plan and arrangement
displayForm: I'm going to get dinner nearby. We're meeting at the noodle place at eight.

ru.translation: Я собираюсь поужинать неподалёку. Мы встречаемся в восемь в лапшичной.

examples.text: I'm going to get dinner nearby. We're meeting at the noodle place at eight.

npcReplyCorrect: Sounds good. I'll look up the menu tonight.

lemma: share a plan involving a different friend
displayForm: I'm going to meet Maya for a walk next week.

ru.translation: На следующей неделе я собираюсь встретиться с Майей и погулять.
ru.usageNote: The variation changes the person in the learner's plan; the NPC remains Alex.

examples.text: I'm going to meet Maya for a walk next week.

npcReplyCorrect: That sounds nice. What day are you meeting?

lemma: give the time and place for a plan with a different friend
displayForm: We're meeting by the river on Wednesday after her class.

ru.translation: Мы встречаемся у реки в среду после её занятия.
ru.usageNote: Present Continuous marks the agreed arrangement with Maya.

examples.text: We're meeting by the river on Wednesday after her class.

npcReplyCorrect: I hope the weather is good for your walk.

lemma: share two plans before one needs to change
displayForm: I'm going to visit the book fair on Thursday, and I'm meeting Maya for dinner on Saturday.

ru.translation: В четверг я собираюсь на книжную ярмарку, а в субботу встречаюсь с Майей за ужином.
ru.usageNote: This variation starts with two distinct plans; the first changes after Alex shares new information.

examples.text: I'm going to visit the book fair on Thursday, and I'm meeting Maya for dinner on Saturday.

npcReplyCorrect: I saw the notice—the book fair opens on Friday this week, not Thursday. Maya says Saturday still works.

lemma: correct one plan after learning a new condition
displayForm: Oh, then I'm going to visit the book fair on Friday instead. I'm still meeting Maya for dinner on Saturday.

ru.translation: Тогда я собираюсь пойти на книжную ярмарку в пятницу. А с Майей мы всё же встречаемся на ужин в субботу.
ru.usageNote: The fair's opening day changes, so the learner adjusts one plan and preserves the other arrangement.

examples.text: Oh, then I'm going to visit the book fair on Friday instead. I'm still meeting Maya for dinner on Saturday.

npcReplyCorrect: All right, enjoy the fair!
